cases.title: Public Premiums
cases.name: Sarah M. London
cases.amount_label: FY2025 reported CEO compensation · includes equity valuations
cases.summary: Centene reported $19.51 million in 2025 compensation for CEO Sarah London. The insurer’s Medicaid business brought in $90.24 billion in premium and service revenue. Its pay formula still produced a cash incentive after the earnings metric missed its target, making the board’s balance of growth, care quality and executive rewards worth examining.
cases.accountability: Follow three separate decisions: what states pay a plan, what the plan spends on care, and what the board awards management. Growth incentives deserve examination alongside quality and access; these records do not establish that any patient was denied care to fund executive compensation.

findings.text: London’s FY2025 SCT totals $19,506,298, including $1,473,077 salary, $2,109,446 annual cash incentive and $15,537,733 grant-date stock value.

The earnings-per-share metric earned zero and carried 60% of the annual incentive weight. Revenue and quality/strategic measures produced a bonus at 71.6% of target. The SEC’s alternative Compensation Actually Paid measure was $4,646,963—about 24% of the Summary Compensation Table total—and also is not cash received.
FY2025 premium/service revenue: Medicaid $90.238B; Medicare $37.210B; Commercial $42.003B; Other $5.130B. The $174.581B total is a revenue measure, not an audited taxpayer-receipts total.

Medicaid is jointly financed by federal and state governments. State agencies contract with plans through monthly capitation; downstream provider payments must not be counted again as additional government spending.

cases.title: Family Stakes
cases.role: Homeland Security secretary since March 24, 2026; former Oklahoma senator
cases.amount_label: Disclosed Botanic Tonics stake; investment value
cases.summary: Markwayne Mullin disclosed a $500,001–$1 million stake in Botanic Tonics, a kratom seller, alongside family real estate and private-company interests. Reporting linked him to efforts that could help the kratom industry; his separate wastewater-company income was estimated at $89,498. DHS says he follows ethics rules and has not lobbied for any individual or company.
cases.accountability: Which official decisions intersected with the businesses he kept, when did he acquire the Botanic Tonics stake, and what recusals protected the public? The company stake and the policy advocacy are both documented; an exact personal gain from those policies has not been measured.

findings.text: The March 2026 filing reports Botanic Tonics at $500,001–$1,000,000, with no income or less than $201. This establishes an exposed financial interest, not a million-dollar payment.

Mullin joined the July 29, 2025 HHS/FDA event announcing action against concentrated 7-OH. FDA explicitly said natural kratom leaf was not the target. On CNN, NYT reporter Kenneth Vogel said Mullin pressed health officials to soften kratom warnings during both Senate and DHS service. The proposed advantage is reduced pressure on the industry in which he invested, rather than a government contract to Botanic Tonics.

Senate Finance ranking member Ron Wyden’s August 3, 2026 letter asked when Mullin acquired the investment and what contacts Botanic Tonics had with officials. Its accusations are an oversight position, not a court finding.

Allotment Services owns an interest in Apres Spectrum, valued at $1,000,001–$5,000,000. The $89,498 business-income-and-interest entry is expressly estimated from a 2024 K-1 because the 2025 K-1 had not been received. The March 17 ethics agreement permits retaining the interest because DHS deemed the likelihood of conflicting matters remote, with a recusal commitment.

Christie has her own identifiable financial result: the CY2024 Senate filing lists Rowan’s Restaurant LLC as a spouse asset with $1,000,001–$5,000,000 in capital gains and reports its full sale on February 27, 2024. The buyer and any public-sector connection are not established by those entries.

The 2024 Senate filing identifies Christie’s spouse assets and joint family interests. The 2026 filing lists six numbered family trusts, each with 3.2% of Mullin Family HoldCo; their values are already included in the holding company’s $5,000,001–$25,000,000 COP Hometown interest. Neither the six trustees nor their beneficiaries are identified by those rows.

Mullin Properties receives interest on an Xtreme Boat & RV note, and Mullin Properties, Mullin Realty and TC 4 Investments report substantial property-income bands. The filing supplies company and property interests but not enough information to identify tenants, public-sector customer revenue, expenses or each family member’s distributions.

The family investment company’s March 2026 holdings included L3Harris and RTX. His ethics agreement required listed securities to be sold within 90 days; a June 24 transaction filing reports June 10 sales of each at $100,001–$250,000. These are historical stock interests and sale values, not a share of the companies’ government awards or measured trading profit.

Napatree Technology received $265.38 million in net federal obligations for AS3, Bumblebee and Hornet systems. The U.S. government record identifies Napatree as the recipient; public reporting links the products and companies, but their ownership and payment chain remain incomplete.
cases.accountability: The Napatree award record identifies one offer, a noncompetitive procurement and an urgency exception. Schmidt’s earlier defense advisory work and Roper’s documented 2024 board role make the decision trail worth examining. The records reviewed do not show either man selected the contractor, waived competition, or received these sums personally.

findings.text: The January agreement was awarded on January 30, 2026. The later May announcement is a three-year IDIQ ceiling, so $500 million is not an established payment or personal enrichment figure.

USAspending lists five actions on W912CH26CA009, all before September 30, totaling $265,382,200 after a deobligation and reobligation cancel. Napatree Technology LLC, UEI H87XAJ4YQJ15, is the legal recipient.

The latest contract data specify one offer, not competed, only one source, urgency under FAR 6.302-2, and firm fixed price. Those fields identify the procurement route; they do not establish an improper award.

The Wall Street Journal identifies Schmidt as a Perennial investor. Forbes traced the earlier White Stork project and its Project Eagle name, plus several related LLCs. Project continuity does not prove all those legal entities are interchangeable.

The Estonian register lists Eric and Wendy Schmidt as indirect beneficial owners of Volya Robotics, with start dates in September 2023 and February 2026. NT Island Holdings is its registered 100% shareholder from February 25, 2026. The route from this company to the U.S. awardee remains unverified.

Ukraine’s presidency identified Schmidt as Swift Beat’s CEO when a drone-production memorandum was signed in July 2025. That confirms an operating role in a related business, not Perennial ownership percentages or U.S. personal proceeds.

Schmidt’s Defense Innovation Board chairmanship ended in 2020; the 2021 congressional hearing identifies his NSCAI chairmanship. Roper was on the Defense Innovation Board in February 2024 and was reported working with the drone project. No reviewed source establishes their involvement in the 2026 selection decisions.
A September Army release separately lists a $500 million Napatree IDIQ. It is retained as an ordering ceiling, without assuming it duplicates or adds to Perennial’s May vehicle.

The Army documented Bumblebee V2 training and assessment with Rangers on July 8, 2026. This is evidence of systems in use, while accepted quantities, full delivery milestones and unit economics remain to be reconciled.

response.text: Army and company announcements describe operationally tested systems and lower-cost counter-drone capabilities. Perennial declined to give DefenseScoop the expected unit count or Middle East performance details. Schmidt declined comment to the March Wall Street Journal report.

cases.confidence_basis: Government announcements and the archived five-action API reconciliation establish the awards, ceiling semantics and Napatree obligations. Investor status is reported by the Wall Street Journal and DefenseScoop; Volya beneficial ownership is a public registry entry. Corporate continuity, attributable profits and decision influence are not established.
cases.missing_fact: The U.S. legal-entity chain and cap tables; May IDIQ identifier; Napatree/Perennial intercompany payments; award justifications and decision contacts; delivery acceptance; Schmidt distributions and Wendy’s economic interest in the U.S. recipient.
